sentences.text: Hello and welcome to the Slow English Podcast. My name is Emili. Today I will talk about a beautiful
city. This city is Athens. Athens is the capital of Greece. Greece is a country in Europe. It is near
the sea and has many islands. Athens is a very old city. It is one of the oldest cities in the
world. People lived in Athens more than 2,500 years ago. That is a very long time. Today,
Athens is a big city. More than 3 million people live there. It is full of history, culture,
and sunshine. Let's talk about some famous places in Athens. The most famous place is the
it is a big hill in the city. On the hill, there are old buildings made of stone.
One building is called the Parthenon. It is a big temple for a Greek goddess named Athena.
Athena gave her name to the city, Athens. From the Acropolis, you can see all of the city.
Many tourists go there every day. They take photos and learn about ancient Greece.
Athens also has many museums. One famous museum is the Acropolis Museum. You can see statues,
pots, and things from a long time ago. Another famous place is Syntagma Square.
It is in the center of the city. There is a big building called the Parliament.
In front of it, there are guards and special clothes. They stand still and change positions
every hour. You can also visit Placa, an old area with small streets. There are shops, cafes,
and houses with flowers. It is a nice place to walk and relax.
Now let's talk about food. Greek food is delicious. People eat olives,
cheese, and bread. They eat musaca, a dish with meat, potatoes, and eggplant. They eat
souvlaki, meat on a stick. And for dessert, people eat baklava, a sweet pastry with nuts and honey.
In Athens, people like to drink coffee. You can see many cafes with people sitting outside.
Athens has hot summers and mild winters. In summer, the sun shines almost every day.
Many people visit Athens in spring and summer. Athens is close to the sea. You can take a bus or
tram to go to the beach. Many people swim and relax near the water. In Athens, people speak Greek.
But many people also speak English, especially in hotels, restaurants, and museums.
People are friendly and happy to help tourists. Athens is the city of history, sunshine, and good food.
It is old and modern at the same time. You can learn, relax, and enjoy life there.

We go to Italy. Our city today is Bologna. Bologna is historic. Bologna is warm. Bologna
is full of life and food. Please relax. Please listen slowly. Let's begin our journey.
Part two, Italy and Europe. Italy is a country in Europe. It is famous all over the world.
Italy has history. Italy has art. Italy has food. Many people visit Italy every year. They come to see
cities. They come to eat Italian food. Bologna is not the capital, but Bologna is very important.
It is a real Italian city. Part three, where is Bologna? Bologna is in the north of Italy.
It is in a region called Emilia Romagna. The city is not near the sea. It is not in the mountains.
It is on flat land. Bologna is easy to reach. Trains come from many cities. People travel here
often. At part four, weather and seasons, Bologna has four seasons. In summer, it is hot. The sun is
strong. In winter, it can be cold. Sometimes there is fog. Spring and autumn are nice.
The weather is soft. People enjoy walking outside. The seasons change slowly. Life changes with the
weather. Part five, a very old city. Bologna is a very old city. People lived here long ago.
The city has Roman history. The city has medieval history. Old buildings are everywhere. Old
streets tell stories. When you walk in Bologna, you walk through history. Part six, the Red City.
Bologna is called the Red City. Many buildings are red. They are made of red bricks. The roofs
are red. The walls are red. When the sun shines, the city looks warm and strong. The color gives
Bologna a special feeling. Part seven, portacos and streets. Bologna is famous for portacos.
Portacos are long covered walkways. You can walk under them. You are safe from sun and rain.
The portacos are very long. They go through the whole city. Walking in Bologna is easy.
Walking feels calm and slow. Part eight, piazza majori. The heart of Bologna is piazza majori.
This is the main square. People meet here. People sit and talk. People enjoy the space.
Big buildings are around the square. Life feels open and social. This place is very important
for the city. At part nine, the old university Bologna has a very famous university. It is
one of the oldest universities in the world. Students come from many countries. They study
many subjects. Young people feel the city. They bring energy and ideas. Because of students,
Bologna feels young and alive. Part 10, food and Bologna. Bologna is famous for food.
People love food here. A famous sauce is bolognese. It is made with meat and tomato.
People eat pasta. People eat bread. People eat together. Food is part of daily life.
Meals are long and social. Part 11, daily life in Bologna.
Daily life in Bologna is active. People work. People study. In the evening, people relax.
They walk in the streets. They sit in cafes. Life is not too fast. Life is not too slow. It feels
balanced. Hello everyone. Welcome to the Slow English Podcast. I am Emily, your host.
Today we are traveling to a small and charming city in South America. It is called Quenca.
Quenca is in Ecuador, a country in the northwest of South America. This city is full of history,
rivers, and friendly people. Let's explore Quenca together. Part 2, where is Quenca?
Quenca is in the Andes Mountains in southern Ecuador. The city is surrounded by hills, rivers,
and green valleys. It is calm and peaceful, perfect for enjoying history and nature.
Part 3, history of Quenca. Quenca has a long history dating back to the Inca civilization.
The Spanish built colonial houses, churches, and plazas here in the 16th century. Walking
in Quenca is like walking through history with beautiful old buildings on every street.
Part 4, main attractions. The main attractions include the New Cathedral, Old Cathedral,
and Plaza Calderon. You can visit museums, art galleries, and small local markets.
The city combines history, architecture, and peaceful natural surroundings.
Part 5, the city of Quenca. Quenca is small but lively. There are cafes, shops, and restaurants.
People walk in the streets, ride bicycles, or take small cars. The city is friendly, safe, and welcoming.
Part 6, food in Quenca. Food in Quenca is fresh and flavorful. People eat potatoes,
corn, meat, and local vegetables. A popular dish is kui, which is roasted guinea pig,
traditional in the Andes. Local sweets, fruits, and chocolate are also very popular.
Part 7, the people of Quenca. People in Quenca are friendly and polite.
They speak Spanish, and some speak English for tourists. Life is calm,
family is important, and traditions are respected. People enjoy festivals, music, and cultural activities.
Part 8, culture and festivals. Quenca has many cultural events and festivals. People celebrate
music, dance, and traditional holidays. Folk music, parades, and religious ceremonies are part of
everyday life. Visitors can enjoy and sometimes join the local celebrations. Part 9, nature
around Quenca. Quenca is surrounded by rivers, mountains, and valleys. You can hike, explore nature,
or enjoy the beautiful views of the city. The air is fresh, and nature is close to the city.
It is perfect for walking, photography, and quiet reflection. Part 10, travel and tourism.
Quenca is reachable by plane, bus, or car from keto or guaya keel. Tourists come to see history,
architecture, and peaceful nature. Tourism helps local people earn money and preserve traditions.
Part 11, daily life in Quenca. Life in Quenca is calm and simple. People wake up early,
go to work or school, and spend time with family. Children play in streets or plazas,
and families enjoy cafes, parks, and riversides. Life is connected to culture, nature, and community.
Part 12, why Quenca is special? Quenca is not a famous city like keto, but it is full of charm,
history, and calm life. It combines colonial architecture, natural beauty, and friendly people
Slow English Podcast. I am Emili, and I hope you enjoyed this journey through Quenca Ecuador.
Today, we will talk about Dublin, the capital city of Ireland. Dublin is the biggest city in Ireland.
It is full of history, music, and friendly people. We will talk about Dublin in four parts. Nature,
city, culture, and daily life. Part 1, nature. Dublin is close to the sea. The river Liffy
runs through the city. You can see many bridges across the river. Dublin also has many green parks.
One of the largest parks is Phoenix Park. It is one of the biggest city parks in Europe.
In the park, you can see deer, walk, cycle, or have a picnic. The weather in Dublin is often rainy and
cloudy, but the rain makes the city green and fresh. In summer, it is mild and not too hot.
In winter, it is cold but not very snowy. Part 2, city Dublin is a mix of old and modern.
The city has many old buildings with beautiful design. One famous place is Trinity College.
It is a very old university. Inside, you can see the Book of Kells, a famous manuscript.
Another important place is Dublin Castle. It has been used for hundreds of years for government
and events. Dublin also has modern areas with shops, cafes, and restaurants. The streets are lively
and you can often hear music from pubs and street performers. Part 3, culture.
Dublin is known for its culture. It is home to many famous writers like James Joyce and Oscar Wilde.
You can visit museums and libraries to learn about Irish literature. Music is everywhere in Dublin.
Traditional Irish music is played in pubs with instruments like the fiddle and the tin whistle.
People enjoy singing, clapping, and dancing to the music.
Food in Dublin is simple but tasty. Traditional dishes include Irish stew and soda bread.
And of course, people enjoy drinking tea, which is very popular in Ireland.
Part 4, Daily Life. Daily life in Dublin is busy but friendly.
People go to work, school, or university. Students from many countries live in Dublin.
The public transport includes buses, trams, and trains. In the evenings, people like to meet friends
and cafes or pubs. They talk, listen to music, and enjoy time together.
On weekends, families go to parks, markets, or visit the seaside. Some people also take short
trips to the countryside near Dublin. Life in Dublin is a mix of tradition and modern style.
It is a city with history, music, and warm people. That is all for today.
Now you know about Dublin's nature, city, culture, and daily life.
It is a beautiful city with parks, history, and music.
Today, we will talk about Dubrovnik, a beautiful city in Croatia. Part 1, Introduction. Dubrovnik
is a historic city on the coast of the Adriatic Sea. It is also called the Pearl of the Adriatic.
The city is famous for its old walls, red roofs, and blue sea. Many tourists visit Dubrovnik
every year. Part 2, Dubrovnik has a very long history. It was an important city for trade in the
Middle Ages. The city was independent for many years and was very rich. The old town is
surrounded by stone walls that are over two kilometers long. These walls protected the city
from enemies. Today, you can walk on the walls and see amazing views of the sea and the city.
Dubrovnik is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Part 3, Old Town and Landmarks.
The Old Town of Dubrovnik has many beautiful places. Stratton Street, the main street with
shops and cafes. Rectors Palace, a historic building, spawns a palace, a famous gothic
and renaissance building. Churches and fountains that show the city's history. The streets are
narrow and full of stone houses with red roofs. It feels like walking back in time.
Part 4, beaches and nature. Dubrovnik is not only about history. It also has beautiful beaches
and clear blue water. Popular beaches are Banja Beach and La Pad Beach. You can swim,
relax and enjoy the sun. Near Dubrovnik, there are small islands like Locrum Island.
People take a boat to visit and enjoy nature. Part 5, food in Dubrovnik. Food is fresh and tasty.
People eat a lot of seafood, like fish, mussels and squid. A popular dish is black risotto,
made with cuttlefish. Another dish is pasticata. Beef cooked with wine and herbs. Fresh fruit,
olive oil and bread are also part of daily meals. Part 6, culture and fun facts. Dubrovnik has many
festivals with music, dance and theater. The most famous one is the Dubrovnik Summer Festival with
concerts and plays. Some fun facts. Dubrovnik was a filming location for the TV series Game
of Thrones. The city walls are some of the best preserved in the world. The Old Town has no cars,
only walking streets. Part 7, weather and tourism. Dubrovnik has a Mediterranean climate. Some
summers are hot and sunny. Winters are mild and rainy. Tourists love to visit in the summer
for beaches and festivals. That is all for today. Now you know many things about Dubrovnik Croatia.
I hope you learned something new today.
